papers.title: Pediatric Sleep Assessment through Spectral Sleep Scoring: A Comparison with Polysomnography
papers.summary: This study validates a spectral sleep scoring method for pediatric sleep (n=192, ages 9-18y), comparing spectral stages with visual AASM-based scoring. High agreement (71-89%, Cohen's kappa=0.76) supports spectral scoring as an efficient tool, also providing additional physiological detail relevant for pediatric populations.

papers.title: On variability in local field potentials.
papers.summary: This study analyzed variability in EEG and local field potentials (LFP), showing that across-trial variance and intra-trial variance (signal power) are nearly identical outside event-related potentials. They introduced CV(power), a mean-normalized variability metric, and found LFP gamma-band power increases after stimulus onset, unlike EEG.

papers.title: RobustSeiz: An Open-Source Framework for Benchmarking the Robustness of EEG Seizure Detection Models
papers.summary: RobustSeiz is an open-source framework for standardized robustness benchmarking of EEG seizure detectors under real-world distribution shifts and adversarial inputs. It standardizes four public EEG corpora (CHB-MIT, TUSZ, Siena, SeizeIT1) and evaluates detector performance across controlled transforms, demonstrating its utility via an AWGN analysis on TUSZ.

papers.title: Clinically altered brain activity may not look like aged brain activity: Implications for brain-age modeling and biomarker strategies.
papers.summary: The study examined brain-age gap (BAG) estimation from EEG spectral power in patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer's disease (AD), finding that models trained on healthy controls systematically underpredict age in clinical populations due to divergent age-related EEG trends, questioning the interpretability of EEG-BAG as a biomarker for individual aging.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence models for automated and semiautomated analysis and interpretation of clinical electroencephalography.
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent research and developments in AI for clinical EEG analysis from a clinical perspective, covering spike/seizure detection, wearable EEG, critically ill patients, epilepsy surgery, and automated interpretation. It highlights the impact of artificial neural networks in bringing AI-based EEG interpretation closer to clinical implementation.

papers.title: EEG Oscillations in Guided Mindfulness versus Mind-Wandering in Young Adults: Effects of Auditory Task Instruction and Naturalistic Video
papers.summary: This study used EEG to compare alpha and theta oscillations during mindfulness versus mind-wandering in 20 non-expert meditators, finding that mindfulness significantly increased posterior alpha power, while theta was larger when auditory instructions were present. The results suggest that acute mindfulness effects are most consistently observed as increases in posterior alpha-band activity.

papers.title: Is Ultra-Long-Term Subscalp EEG Ready to Go "Solo"? Transforming the Landscape of Antiseizure Medication Management.
papers.summary: This editorial commentary discusses the potential of ultra-long-term subscalp EEG to transform antiseizure medication management, despite the abstract being empty. It likely argues for the clinical utility of this technology.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal Dynamics of the Flow Experience: An EEG Microstate Analysis.
papers.summary: This study used EEG microstate analysis in 43 participants during a video game to examine flow states, finding that flow was associated with reduced duration and frequency of microstates C and E, which are linked to default mode network activity. This supports the idea that flow involves diminished self-referential processing.

papers.title: Breathable, Biocompatible, Ultrathin Bilayer Epidermal Electrodes for Long-Term and Motion-Artifact-Resistant Monitoring ofHigh-Fidelity Electrophysiological Signals.
papers.summary: This study introduces a breathable, biocompatible, ultrathin bilayer epidermal electrode for long-term, motion-artifact-resistant electrophysiological monitoring, demonstrating high-fidelity acquisition of EMG, EOG, EEG, and ECG signals. The electrode achieves reliable muscle fatigue assessment and gesture recognition, offering a strategy for stable low-impedance interfaces.

papers.title: Revisiting the concept that interictal implies asymptomatic: Pulse wave amplitude drops uncover autonomic responses during generalized paroxysmal fast activities.
papers.summary: This study analyzed 511 generalized paroxysmal fast activities (GPFA) during sleep in 21 epilepsy patients using polysomnography and pulse wave amplitude drops (PWAD) as an autonomic marker. It found that 40.5% of clinically silent GPFA were associated with PWAD≥30%, indicating autonomic activation, challenging the asymptomatic notion of interictal discharges.

papers.title: Analysis of EEG microstate transition patterns and multi-instance learning-based recognition model for depression.
papers.summary: This study proposes a rule-driven EEG microstate sequence analysis framework for depression recognition, using the RuleGrowth algorithm to mine discriminative transition rules integrated into an attention-based multiple instance learning model. The method outperformed static feature approaches, achieving accuracies up to 96.67% on the MODMA dataset, and identified significant group differences in higher-order transition patterns, suggesting disrupted brain-state switching in MDD.

papers.title: Implant-Grade Neural Sensing with Artifact-Resilient Computational Intelligence Preserves Spatial Fidelity of HFO Biomarkers in Epilepsy.
papers.summary: The paper evaluates a wireless implantable neural interface for preserving high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) in epilepsy monitoring. The system retained ~82% of clinical HFOs and localized the seizure onset zone with 84% sensitivity and 90% specificity.

papers.title: Detecting Interbrain Synchronization in EEG Hyperscanning with MUSE-S EEG headban
papers.summary: This study classifies EEG hyperscanning data from MUSE-S consumer EEG headbands during a two-person Tetris game versus relaxation. Using spectral and cross-coherence features with a CNN, it achieved perfect discrimination with full features and 94%/79% accuracy with only inter-subject coherence features for training/test, indicating interbrain synchronization.

papers.title: EEG spectral analysis of nighttime sleep and daytime MSLTs and neurocognitive evaluations in obstructive sleep apnea patients with residual sleepiness.
papers.summary: This case-control study compared EEG spectral power and neurocognitive performance in OSA patients with residual excessive sleepiness (RES) versus those without. RES patients showed increased delta/theta and decreased alpha/beta power, along with impairments in executive function, processing speed, working memory, and attention, suggesting that RES involves sleep-wake dysregulation and distinct neurophysiological correlates.

papers.title: Mice and humans use ambiguous local motion to stabilize gaze
papers.summary: The authors investigated whether ambiguous local motion signals can directly drive reflexive gaze stabilization in mice and humans, using electrophysiology, modeling, and eye tracking. They found that eye movements follow local motion even when it dissociates from global object motion, indicating a conserved sensorimotor heuristic that prioritizes local cues.

papers.title: Stimulation selectively blocks subthalamic high β-cortical high γ coupling in Parkinson's disease.
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This study in Parkinson's disease patients examined subthalamic beta-cortical gamma phase-amplitude coupling under subthalamic stimulation at varying levels. Stimulation selectively reduced high beta-high gamma coupling, correlating with improved bradykinesia, suggesting a mechanism involving task-specific hyperdirect pathway modulation.

papers.title: Oscillatory Traveling Waves During Visual Entrainment in Autistic and Non-Autistic Adults.
papers.journal: Autism : the international journal of research and practice
papers.summary: The study investigated EEG traveling waves during visual entrainment in autistic and non-autistic adults. Non-autistic participants showed increased backward (top-down) waves, while autistic participants showed a pronounced increase in forward (sensory) waves, supporting predictive coding accounts of autistic perception.

papers.title: Frequency and laminar profile of feature-specific visual activity revealed by interleaved EEG-fMRI.
papers.summary: This study used interleaved EEG-fMRI to examine the laminar relationship between cortical oscillations and visual feature processing. They found that gamma activity positively correlates with feature-specific BOLD in superficial layers, while alpha band power shows both feature-unspecific and feature-specific correlations across layers, suggesting alpha oscillations play a role in active stimulus processing rather than just inhibition.

papers.title: Hippocampal Seizure-Related Burden is Associated with Accelerated Long-Term Forgetting in Focal Epilepsy.
papers.summary: This study introduced cumulative hippocampal seizure-related burden metrics in focal epilepsy patients and examined their association with long-term memory consolidation. Higher burden in the dominant hippocampus was associated with poorer verbal memory consolidation at one week, independent of seizure frequency and structural pathology, suggesting cumulative ictal-postictal dysfunction is a major predictor of memory impairment.

papers.title: Wearable Sleep and Circadian Monitoring in Intensive Care Nursing: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review assessed wearable sleep/circadian monitoring in intensive care across 61 reports. Wearables were feasible but showed variable accuracy, especially poor wake specificity in immobile patients, and they complement but cannot replace clinical assessment for sleep evaluation.

papers.title: Exploring EEG and ECG in Music Listening: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review examined 18 peer-reviewed studies using simultaneous EEG and ECG during passive music listening in healthy adults. Findings were heterogeneous and lacked integration, highlighting methodological inconsistencies and a need for standardized guidelines to study brain-heart interactions in music.

papers.title: Hearing Aid Noise Reduction Algorithms Support Neural Speech Tracking by Enhancing Spectrotemporal Consistency of Phase-Locked Brain Responses to Acoustic Edges.
papers.summary: This study investigated how hearing aid noise reduction (NR) affects neural speech tracking in hearing-impaired listeners. NR partially restored P1 amplitudes to acoustic edges in noisy conditions and improved spectrotemporal consistency of phase-locked responses, correlating with enhanced envelope tracking, suggesting NR supports speech encoding by restoring neural responses to acoustic edges.

papers.title: From screens to live interactions: Considerations for naturalistic EEG paradigms in social and affective neuroscience.
papers.summary: This review examines analytic variability in live, naturalistic EEG paradigms in social and affective neuroscience, identifying five varying analytic approaches and showing in infant data that different approaches can change EEG results. It recommends standards and best practices for reporting analytic decisions to improve transparency and replicability.

papers.title: The effect of BIS-guided sevoflurane anesthesia on postoperative nausea and vomiting in pediatric adenoidectomy: a prospective randomized controlled trial.
papers.journal: Sao Paulo medical journal = Revista paulista de medicina
papers.summary: This prospective randomized controlled trial in 58 children undergoing adenoidectomy found that BIS-guided sevoflurane anesthesia reduced postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) within 24 hours compared with standard care, and also lowered sevoflurane consumption and emergence time. BIS-guided anesthesia was independently associated with lower odds of PONV.

papers.title: Peripheral immune-metabolic markers and quantitative EEG in drug-naïve first-episode mania: A case-control study.
papers.summary: This case-control study compared drug-naïve first-episode mania patients to healthy controls, finding higher monocyte counts, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, and lower albumin, along with increased absolute spectral power in nine brain region-band cells. Lower albumin was associated with higher frontal and central beta power, though associations did not survive multiple comparison correction.

papers.title: GCaMP fiber photometry reveals mechanistic insights into focused ultrasound neuromodulation in acute seizures.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of acute seizures, low-intensity focused ultrasound (FUS) attenuated epileptic calcium transients and ECoG spikes for up to 40 minutes, with reduced c-Fos expression co-localized with NMDAR2B and GAD65/67. These findings suggest FUS exerts calcium-dependent anti-seizure effects by modulating excitatory-inhibitory balance, with GCaMP fiber photometry as a mechanistic surrogate.

papers.title: Psilocybin prevents chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy through mitochondrial trafficking preservation.
papers.summary: This study shows that two doses of psilocybin before chemotherapy durably prevented chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy in platinum- and taxane-based models without impairing antitumor efficacy. Psilocybin preserved axonal mitochondrial trafficking via the TrkB-Akt-PAK5-MAP2-KIF5B pathway and normalized central neural activity, supporting its potential as a prophylactic for CIPN.

papers.title: Elevated neuronal excitability and seizure susceptibility in a mouse model of SCN2A-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
papers.summary: This study generated a novel Scn2aE430A mouse model and found hippocampal pyramidal neurons are hyperexcitable, with enhanced long-term potentiation and recurrent epileptiform discharges but no spontaneous seizures. Prenatal phenytoin improved seizure outcomes in seizure-induction assays, establishing the model as clinically relevant and pharmacologically tractable for SCN2A-related DEE.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of Changes in Brain Activity Among Edentulous Patients Rehabilitated With Conventional Complete Dentures and Tooth-Supported Overdentures Using Electroencephalography: An In Vivo Study.
papers.summary: This prospective observational study compared EEG-based brain activity in 36 edentulous patients rehabilitated with conventional complete dentures, tooth-supported overdentures without attachments, and with stud attachments. After two months, all three groups showed significant increases in EEG-derived cortical activity, with no significant between-group differences, indicating that restoration of masticatory function is associated with enhanced cortical electrical activity regardless of prosthesis type.

papers.title: Safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of intravenously administered deuterated N,N-dimethyltryptamine (CYB004) in healthy volunteers.
papers.summary: This exploratory randomized controlled study in healthy volunteers assessed the safety, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of intravenously administered deuterated DMT (CYB004). It found that CYB004 had a pharmacodynamic profile similar to DMT but with a two-fold longer half-life, prolonging psychedelic effects, while maintaining an acceptable safety profile at clinically relevant exposures despite moderate to high pharmacokinetic variability.

papers.title: Preoperative Atrial Electrophysiology in Pediatric Tetralogy of Fallot Compared with Ventricular Septal Defect.
papers.summary: Compared preoperative atrial epicardial electrophysiology between pediatric TOF and VSD patients, finding that TOF patients had lower voltages and more conduction abnormalities in the left atrium and pulmonary veins despite less LA dilatation, suggesting inherent atrial substrate differences that may explain higher postoperative arrhythmia risk.

papers.title: Natural history and clinical impact of epilepsy in adults with Down syndrome: a multicentre clinical study.
papers.summary: In a multicentre longitudinal study of 4804 adults with Down syndrome, active epilepsy incidence rose sharply after symptomatic Alzheimer's disease onset (56.9% at 9 years), and LOMEDS was associated with increased mortality and faster cognitive decline.

papers.title: Chronic social instability stress differentially affects the behavior and the transcriptome of the anterodorsal bed nucleus of the stria terminalis between male and female mice
keywords: bed nucleus of the stria terminalis
papers.summary: Chronic social instability stress in mice caused opposite behavioral effects in males (more avoidant) and females (less avoidant), with sex-specific transcriptomic changes in the anterodorsal BNST and altered CRH neuron properties only in males.

papers.title: Patterns and Clinical Predictors of Antiseizure Medication Use in Pediatric Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.summary: This multi-center retrospective cohort study of 467 pediatric TBI patients identified clinical predictors of antiseizure medication (ASM) prescription during hospitalization and at discharge. Intracranial injury on imaging, moderate Glasgow Coma Scale score, admission to neurology/neurosurgery, and immediate seizures were associated with inpatient ASM use; neuroimaging abnormalities and immediate seizures predicted discharge ASM prescription.

papers.title: Comparative study of chlorophyll measurement in Physcomitrium patens moss using a conventional microscope adapted for combined 2D+1D imaging and spectral analysis
papers.summary: This preprint describes a simple method for attaching a miniature fiber spectrometer to a conventional microscope to enable combined 2D imaging and 1D spectral analysis. The authors demonstrated the setup's performance for quantitative chlorophyll measurement in Physcomitrium patens moss, comparing color imaging and spectral sampling approaches.

papers.title: Electrical Signatures of Life: A Review of Cell Electrophysiology and Dielectric Analysis (2015-2026).
papers.summary: This review covers 2015-2026 literature on cell electrophysiology and dielectric analysis, focusing on label-free cellular electrical signatures (e.g., membrane capacitance, polarizability) and their applications in clinical diagnosis, drug development, and bioprocessing.

papers.title: Shielding the First 24 Postnatal Months of Life: A Proposal for a Prospective Cohort Study of Early-Life Electromagnetic Exposure and Autism Risk.
papers.summary: This protocol proposes a prospective cohort study to test whether reducing electromagnetic radiation exposure during the first 24 postnatal months, via sleep-phase Faraday shielding, can reduce autism risk, with exploratory genomic and EEG endpoints.

papers.title: Multidimensional maturation of oxytocin neurons: A principal component analysis of postnatal development.
papers.summary: The paper investigates postnatal maturation of oxytocin neurons in the rat paraventricular nucleus using electrophysiology and principal component analysis, revealing a dynamic reorganization through distinct functional states. A 'high-gain' state around day 7 suggests a critical window for circuit refinement.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Mobile-Delivered Exercise and Yoga Programs on Depressive Symptom Reduction in Employees: Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial compared 12-session mobile-delivered adaptive exercise and yoga programs against a cognitive behavioral therapy-based self-care control for reducing depressive symptoms and stress in 75 employees. The yoga group showed significantly greater improvement in depressive symptoms at 4-week follow-up compared to control and exhibited sustained improvement in cognitive stress responses, while exercise showed more modest, less sustained effects.

papers.title: Case Report: SMART syndrome mimicking Todd's paralysis after meningioma irradiation.
papers.summary: Reported a case of SMART syndrome in a patient with prior meningioma irradiation, presenting with stroke-like symptoms and seizures, with a shorter latency than typical. Diagnosis required exclusion of other causes and treatment with steroids and amlodipine led to improvement.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
